official_document.unsupported_RBW: Features note printed4 / PDF13; DP printed6 and SP printed18
facts: 138K does not support Read-before-Write write mode.
SDPB/SDPX9B support only Normal write mode; READ_MODE chooses bypass vs an extra output pipeline.
The SDP note prohibits a cross-port read and write at the same address, defined by physical14bit AD[13:4]. Same clock does not waive the note.

vendor_library.interpretation: The functional model has nonblocking storage updates and can deterministically simulate old-data collisions; that is not a silicon timing or legal-operation guarantee.

consumers.condition: Writes are issued only from delayed P_A/P_B; reads only during P_C/P_D. P_FLUSH counts16 through0 between phases.
consumers.status: Plausible source-level exclusion, parent companion review owns complete pipeline/physical-granule proof; not accepted merely from these anchors.
consumers.requirement: Prove no actual write-enable overlaps read-enable, including phase drain/reset, before mapping; then address granularity cannot create a cross-port conflict.

consumers.condition: sl_we only in S_U3; sl_re only in S_UC0, both registered default0 every clock.
consumers.status: Distinct state phases with a read-wait gap; parent companion review owns complete reachable-state proof.
consumers.requirement: Prove sl_we && sl_re is unreachable at the RAM edge, including reset/pending registered control.

consumers.condition: Writer accepts inj_we independently of ia/iv1/iv2; i_re streams ioff. iwp resets at last-byte scheduling, before all read pipeline registers drain.
consumers.status: No hardware exclusion. A caller can write a physical conflict group while streaming, and following-packet writes must respect the drain.
consumers.requirement: Prove the actual mailbox bus/firmware producer never writes while read-active or drain; otherwise arbitrate/store accepted writes or change protocol without dropping/duplicating them. Current source-only read-first test is insufficient.

consumers.condition: Actual top txb_re is tied1. RAM writes each TX_DATA transaction while twp not full; reset readback index0 and first TX word0 already conflict.
consumers.status: Concrete normal-use unwanted cross-port collision; must change before the one combined SYN.
consumers.needed_read_edges: For a TXB_Q read accepted at nav_subsystem B_IDLE edgeE0, read RAM at E0; original B_RF edgeE1 captures rf_rdata and acknowledges. B_RF is the actual TX_DATA write edge of a separate serialized transaction.
consumers.minimal_proposal: Replace always-on read with B_IDLE && bus_req && !bus_we && aligned(bus_addr)==RA_MBX_TXB_Q; leave r_MBX_TXB_ADDR as address. Since all TX writes arise from rf_wr at B_RF and one bus transaction is active, prove WE&&RE==0 independent of physical address width.
consumers.miter: Exercise TX_DATA writes, TXB_ADDR changes, immediate next legal TXB_Q reads, heldreq, two-master arbitration, reset, twp limit/wrap and ACK gaps. Compare bus_ack/bus_rdata and all committed words; check actual CEA/CEB and ADA[13:4]/ADB[13:4]. Pending previous-transaction rf_wr must be included, not assumed absent.

consumers.condition: Each lane read-enable is tied1; con_ra remains at last debug word, while independent CPU console stores append and wrap. Matching physical row groups can collide even if logical byte addresses differ.
consumers.status: Concrete independent-port risk. Valid-read gating alone does not remove a write at the demanded read edge.
consumers.needed_read_edges: Debug E0 (d_st0): capture con_ra; E1 (d_st1): read target; E2 (d_st3): capture con_q and original ACK. E0/E2 dummy reads are unnecessary. CPU con_we is an independent port.
consumers.minimal_proposal: Use read only at valid console d_st1. Give that single edge read priority; if a CPU log write is accepted at it, capture8bit data +10bit wordaddr +2bit lane +valid and commit at E2 when no read is needed. Keep original con_wp/per_ready at E1. Deferring all writes at the demanded read edge avoids any assumption about physical collision granularity.
consumers.why_one_entry_may_suffice: con_we implies req && sel_per, so per_ready becomes1 after E1; at E2 req=mem_valid&&!mem_ready is0, leaving the queued commit uncontended. This is a source argument requiring bus miter, not a completed implementation/proof.
consumers.miter: Compare debug ACK/data at unchanged E2 against old read-first behavior; CPU per_ready/con_wp/log contents; E0/E1/E2 byte writes for all4lanes, same logical word and adjacent physical row words, last4095byte wrap, concurrent CPU/UART/debug heldreq, reset/HOLD and accepted pending-write drain. Do not cancel an already-ACKed write on reset: old RAM had no reset and had already committed it.

actual_stage3_checklist: Reject DPB/DPX9B/SP/SPX9 with any WRITE_MODE=2 before PNR; do not repair a netlist parameter without re-proving source behavior.
Confirm actual target instance geometry, source/physical wide split, INIT and enabled one-cycle read/hold; READ_MODE0 bypass does not mean asynchronous public read.

For each physical write/read pair prove no simultaneous enabled conflict group: CEA && CEB && BLKSEL-match && ADA[13:4]==ADB[13:4] must be unreachable, including adjacent logical addresses folded to the same physical row.
Re-run bus/consumer miters on any RDEN gating or write deferral. A suppressed demanded read or an ignored collision output is not a preservation proof.
Read-only trig/bias/weight leaves must have actual write enables disabled; future mapped primitive tests check initialization and latency but cannot authorize prohibited collision use.
selected_injection_action: Keep u_injb distributed: remove only its STAGE2B_BLOCK opt-in in new consumer candidates. Preserve all INJ_DATA/GO/length/ACK behavior and capacity; do not invent a busy/error protocol just to force the migration.
